title: Automated Texture Patching & Conflict Resolution
who_benefits: Individually-owned artists using Unreal or Unity for personal projects
job_to_be_done: Automatically detect and repair overlapping textures across ten rendering passes without external tools
why_this_design: Runs entirely on local GPU with digest identity preventing recomputation, ensuring privacy and speed
biggest_risk: Latency in local digest sync if network-like dependencies emerge
author_lens: an on-device, privacy-first user who will not send project files anywhere.

title: Local Scene Evolution via Iterative Refinement
who_benefits: Small indie studios optimizing assets for mobile platforms
job_to_be_done: Iteratively refine scene layers using filler logic to remove holes and conflicts, guided by neighbour context without cloud upload
why_this_design: Tetris-like bottom-up clearing with deterministic checks ensures stability and zero data leakage
biggest_risk: Over-iteration if tile digest identities are misaligned
author_lens: an on-device, privacy-first user who will not send project files anywhere.

title: Privacy-First Asset Restoration & Recombination
who_benefits: Archival-focused creators preserving old scenes on personal devices
job_to_be_done: Recombine fragmented layers from memory or backup snapshots using localized rendering and conflict fixing
why_this_design: Each tile carries neighbour context and digest ID—no files ever leave the machine, preserving ownership
biggest_risk: Incomplete rebuild if Neural Engine fails to capture full context
author_lens: an on-device, privacy-first user who will not send project files anywhere.

title: Open provenance sidecars for Unreal Movie Render Graph and Unity Recorder
who_benefits: Unreal and Unity pipeline TDs, compositors, Blender/Nuke/Houdini users, archive teams, and QA engineers
job_to_be_done: Consume each promoted frame, layer, and pass as a trusted, diffable, re-openable artifact in other tools without re-rendering or trusting opaque exports.
why_this_design: Atomic promotion, tile digest identity, verification as a commit gate, and provenance create a stable downstream contract. This idea does not depend on generative AI; it is most valuable for deterministic engine renders and open tooling.
requires: A versioned NDJSON or JSON sidecar with tile coordinates, layer names, digest, lease, node identity, verdicts, EXR/DPX references, color space, camera, timecode, and journal references, plus export adapters for Unreal Movie Render Graph and Unity Recorder.
biggest_risk: Format sprawl and incomplete engine metadata could make sidecars too large or too weak to support reliable debugging in other tools.
evidence_or_analogy: OpenEXR, USD, Alembic, OpenLineage, and Tractor or Deadline event logs show that render outputs need durable provenance to be consumed outside the producing tool.
author_lens: open-source tooling maintainer focused on file formats, interoperability, and letting other tools consume engine outputs

title: Open durable queue protocol for local heterogeneous render farms
who_benefits: Indie studios, CI runners, plugin authors, home Mac and PC users, and open-source farm tools such as Tractor, Deadline, or OpenCue
job_to_be_done: Submit Unreal and Unity render jobs to Mac GPUs, Apple Neural Engines, and PC GPUs over LAN with leases, expiry recovery, admission budgets, and an interactive reserve.
why_this_design: The durable queue, lease recovery, SoC-style hardware direction, and interactive reserve are reusable even for normal rendering. This idea does not depend on layered generation or model lanes; it can be valuable in release 1.
requires: An open queue API using a Job, Layer, Frame hierarchy, node heartbeat, lease expiry, sandbox policy, device capability and budget metadata, journal replay, and thin Unreal and Unity job adapters.
biggest_risk: Engine process isolation, sandboxing, and OS permission constraints on macOS and Windows may make cross-device execution harder than the queue design assumes.
evidence_or_analogy: OpenCue's Job, Layer, Frame model with leases, RenderMan XPU placement, and Tractor or Deadline show that durable, lease-based scheduling is already a useful open-source pattern.
author_lens: open-source tooling maintainer focused on file formats, interoperability, and letting other tools consume engine outputs

title: Layered code artifact format for Unreal and Unity plugin generation
who_benefits: Unreal C++ and Blueprint plugin maintainers, Unity C# plugin maintainers, open-source CI systems, code reviewers, IDE tooling, linters, and test runners
job_to_be_done: Consume generated plugin code as ten verified layers so external tools can patch, audit, test, or reject only the failing layer instead of treating output as one opaque blob.
why_this_design: The tile loop, apron, digest identity, verification as a commit gate, and independent reviewer make code outputs replayable and auditable. This idea depends on release 2 model lanes; without them it is only a code patch format.
requires: A code layer manifest mapping tiles to files, functions, Blueprints, or C# members; AST and diff metadata; test manifests; license and dependency data; deterministic checks such as compile, unit tests, static analysis, and API contract checks; independent reviewer verdicts; and export to patch or JSON plus journal entries.
biggest_risk: Unreal and Unity plugin code is highly context-dependent, and the apron may not capture enough engine API state, so generated code may pass local checks but fail in larger projects.
evidence_or_analogy: Bazel Build Event Stream, Git patches, OpenLineage, GitHub Actions artifacts, and independent review bots show that code provenance, deterministic checks, and separate review verdicts are useful to open tooling.
author_lens: open-source tooling maintainer focused on file formats, interoperability, and letting other tools consume engine outputs

title: Render recipe and tile journal interchange for render graphs
who_benefits: Unreal RDG authors, Unity Render Graph authors, open-source renderers such as Blender, Cycles, or RenderMan, pipeline debugging tools, and visual regression CI
job_to_be_done: Import, diff, replay, or port a verified render graph and tile journal across tools so a pass failure can be reproduced without the original engine scene or source project.
why_this_design: Digest identity from inputs, recipe, apron, and attempt, bottom-up row promotion, and atomic promotion give a stable replayable graph. A plain pass journal would be useful even without generative AI, but the design makes it more trustworthy.
requires: A neutral recipe IR with pass graph, tile grid, apron, camera, light, material, and buffer inputs; a journal of promoted attempts; import and export for Unreal RDG and Unity Render Graph; EXR, USD, and JSON containers; and deterministic visual diff and seam checks.
biggest_risk: Proprietary engine graph formats and driver-specific passes may make the neutral IR incomplete, forcing users to keep engine-side copies of state.
evidence_or_analogy: Unreal RDG, Unity Render Graph, RenderMan RDL, Cycles, and OpenUSD all point toward graph or layered representation; a journal interchange is analogous to OpenImageIO or RenderMan archive for execution provenance.
author_lens: open-source tooling maintainer focused on file formats, interoperability, and letting other tools consume engine outputs

title: Pluggable verification and reviewer verdict API for open QA tools
who_benefits: Open-source QA maintainers, compositing tools, accessibility and color QA tools, CI systems, plugin authors, and independent reviewer model authors
job_to_be_done: Attach, replace, or consume verification checks and independent reviewer verdicts as portable artifacts so external tools can gate promotion, audit quality, or rerun checks without the Nisi engine.
why_this_design: The design separates deterministic validity from independent quality review and stores verdicts with provenance. It does not depend on a specific model; open-source checkers and review bots can plug in.
requires: A verdict schema with deterministic check IDs, thresholds, reviewer model version, tile or frame scope, confidence, failures, and provenance; a sandboxed checker and reviewer plugin API; export to CI logs, EXR metadata, USD metadata, and journal entries; and a policy for reviewer independence.
biggest_risk: Too many verdicts can create alert fatigue, and reviewer models may be non-deterministic or biased, so check IDs, calibration, and independence rules must be stable.
evidence_or_analogy: CI quality gates, OpenLineage metrics, RenderMan or XPU placement constraints, and independent code review bots show that verdicts are consumable scheduling and quality metadata, not just human notes.
author_lens: open-source tooling maintainer focused on file formats, interoperability, and letting other tools consume engine outputs

title: Offline, deterministic VFX shot revision with full provenance
who_benefits: Indie VFX artists and small studios doing iterative shot work (e.g., game cinematics, short films)
job_to_be_done: Revise a single frame or layer (e.g., fix a shadow artifact in the reflection pass) without re-rendering the entire frame or losing track of what changed and why
why_this_design: The tile loop + digest identity + atomic promotion + journal replay means changing one layer (e.g., lighting) only re-runs affected tiles; aprons prevent seams; verification as commit gate ensures no invalid state propagates; provenance is built-in, not bolted on
requires: Release 1 (durable queue, verification, provenance, pass export)
biggest_risk: Digest collisions or apron misalignment causing visible seams in high-contrast edges—mitigated by deterministic tile identity and apron-aware verification
evidence_or_analogy: Like Git’s diff + rebase for VFX: only changed tiles are recomputed, and every change is traceable to a specific digest; analogous to Nuke’s frame-accurate revision with full node history, but deterministic and tiled
author_lens: local-first engineer who runs everything on their own machines and distrusts cloud render services

title: Offline, interactive lighting iteration with real-time feedback on GPU/NPU hybrid
who_benefits: Game developers using Unreal/Unity who need to tweak lighting without waiting for full frame renders or cloud queue time
job_to_be_done: Adjust light intensity or material albedo and see the updated frame in <2 seconds on a local Mac/PC with mixed hardware (e.g., Intel GPU + Apple Neural Engine)
why_this_design: SoC-style hardware direction assigns small, fast filler models to the Neural Engine for hole-filling within layers, while the GPU handles the main render; interactive reserve ensures low-latency jobs skip queue; tile loop with aprons enables partial-frame updates without seams; verification only triggers on confidence thresholds, skipping full re-verify during interactive mode
biggest_risk: Hardware heterogeneity causing timing mismatches between filler and main render—mitigated by admission budgets and sandboxed node isolation
evidence_or_analogy: Like Blender’s EEVEE with real-time lighting, but with layered fidelity and deterministic fallback: if the Neural Engine fills a hole in the depth pass, the result is verified and committed atomically, not left as a guess
author_lens: local-first engineer who runs everything on their own machines and distrusts cloud render services

title: Automated, verifiable test rendering for CI pipelines (no human review)
who_benefits: CI/CD teams in game studios or VFX shops running automated builds (e.g., after shader or level changes)
job_to_be_done: Run a full frame render, compare it against a reference digest, and fail the build only if there’s a *real* visual regression—not a benign change like lighting noise
why_this_design: Verification is deterministic (not model-based), so regressions are binary; row-line commit gate ensures all layers are consistent before promotion; provenance lets you diff two builds’ tile digests to pinpoint the exact layer/tile that changed; reviewer independence means no subjective bias in pass/fail
biggest_risk: Overly strict verification rejecting valid artistic changes (e.g., intentional lighting tweak)—mitigated by configurable verification thresholds per layer
evidence_or_analogy: Like Jest’s snapshot testing, but for pixel data: the digest is the snapshot; aprons ensure tile boundaries don’t cause false positives; similar to Cycles’ test rendering but with deterministic, layer-wise commit gates
author_lens: local-first engineer who runs everything on their own machines and distrusts cloud render services

title: Offline, reproducible AI-assisted asset generation with audit trail
who_benefits: Solo developers generating assets (e.g., textures, props) for internal use without sending data to cloud
job_to_be_done: Generate a texture atlas for a character using local models, then verify it meets constraints (e.g., UV continuity, no seams), and later audit exactly which model version, seed, and inputs produced it
why_this_design: The layered render queue separates intent (e.g., “UV-unwrapped, seamless”) from implementation (e.g., “diffuse + normal + roughness”); filler models fix gaps/conflicts on-device; digest identity + journal replay ensures reproducibility; reviewer independence means a separate model judges quality (e.g., “is this texture tileable?”) without the generator seeing the verdict
biggest_risk: Filler models introducing artifacts in apron regions—mitigated by apron-aware verification and tile-level confidence checks
evidence_or_analogy: Like Docker’s layer caching + reproducible builds, but for generative assets: each tile’s digest is the layer hash; aprons act like build context; reviewer independence mirrors static analysis tools that don’t modify code
author_lens: local-first engineer who runs everything on their own machines and distrusts cloud render services

title: Offline, fault-tolerant long-frame renders (e.g., 10k frames) with resume from last verified tile
who_benefits: Animators rendering long sequences (e.g., cutscenes, VFX shots) on unstable hardware (laptop on battery, shared workstation)
job_to_be_done: Render a 5-minute sequence over days, pausing/resuming without losing progress or re-rendering verified tiles—even after a crash or power loss
why_this_design: Durable queue with leases + expiry recovery ensures jobs aren’t lost on node failure; tile identity (digest) + atomic promotion means only unverified tiles are requeued; row-line commit gate ensures partial frames aren’t committed; provenance journal lets you replay from last known-good state
biggest_risk: Lease expiry during long-running filler model jobs—mitigated by per-job lease extension and sandboxed node health checks
evidence_or_analogy: Like OpenCue’s job recovery, but tile-level: if a node dies mid-tile, the lease expires and the tile is requeued; unlike OpenCue, tiles are immutable and replayable via digest, so no re-computation of verified work
author_lens: local-first engineer who runs everything on their own machines and distrusts cloud render services
